dockerfile_issues.issue: Container runs as root (no USER directive)
dockerfile_issues.detail: Without a USER directive the app process runs as UID 0. Any RCE in Flask, the model-loading code or a dependency gives the attacker root inside the container, making container escape and tampering with model files and secrets far easier.
dockerfile_issues.recommendation: Create an unprivileged user (e.g. RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 app), chown only the paths the app must write, and add USER app before CMD.

dockerfile_issues.issue: Base image not pinned to a SHA256 digest
dockerfile_issues.detail: 'FROM python:3.11-slim' uses a mutable tag. Each build may pull a different image, so builds are not reproducible and a compromised or re-pushed tag would flow straight into production.
dockerfile_issues.recommendation: Pin the base image by digest (FROM python:3.11-slim@sha256:<digest>) and update it deliberately via an automated PR (Dependabot/Renovate).

dockerfile_issues.issue: COPY . copies entire build context (possible secret leakage)
dockerfile_issues.detail: 'COPY . /app' copies the whole build context into the image and no .dockerignore exists. Secrets, .git history, datasets and local checkpoints can be baked into an image layer, where anyone who can pull the image can read them. Secret files present in the context: rag_chatbot\.env.
dockerfile_issues.recommendation: Add a .dockerignore (.env, .git, *.pt, data/, __pycache__/) and COPY only the directories the service needs (e.g. COPY rag_chatbot/ ./rag_chatbot/). Inject secrets at runtime via the orchestrator's secret store.

dockerfile_issues.detail: Orchestrators cannot tell a hung or crashed service from a healthy one, so failures (or a tampered process) can go unnoticed.
dockerfile_issues.recommendation: Add a HEALTHCHECK against the existing /health endpoint, e.g. HEALTHCHECK CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:5001/health')" || exit 1

dockerfile_issues.issue: Build tools left in production image
dockerfile_issues.detail: build-essential, gcc are installed in the single runtime stage. A compiler lets an attacker build exploits in place, and the toolchain (binutils, linux-libc-dev, ...) accounts for most of the image's CVEs.
dockerfile_issues.recommendation: Use a multi-stage build: compile/install wheels in a builder stage and COPY only the installed site-packages into a clean slim (or distroless) runtime stage.

dockerfile_issues.detail: curl, git are not needed at runtime. They give an attacker ready-made tools to download payloads, exfiltrate data and move laterally, and add their own CVEs.
dockerfile_issues.recommendation: Remove them from the runtime image (install in the builder stage only if needed) and use a Python-based HEALTHCHECK instead of curl.
